title: Premvati v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Shashi Kant Gupta, J.; Neeraj Tiwari, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed for failure to appear under Clause 6.8.
headnote: A second writ seeking quashing of a later departmental notice and restoration of supply was dismissed where the consumer had not appeared before the Executive Engineer on the date fixed under an earlier order relegating a theft-based demand to Clause 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The Court held there was no justification to interfere on the same cause of action.
facts: Premvati sought quashing of a 22 October 2019 notice of the Executive Engineer, Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd., Kiravali, Agra, and restoration of her electricity connection. She had earlier challenged an 18 December 2018 demand of Rs. 7,02,500 after inspection alleged theft by 'Katiya' from the main line. Writ-C No. 3942 of 2019 was disposed of on 5 February 2019 directing her to appear before the Executive Engineer on 13 February 2019 under Clause 6.8. The Department said she failed to appear as directed.

holding_units.topic: second writ after failure to appear at directed Clause 6.8 hearing
holding_units.holding: Where an earlier writ against a theft-based electricity demand was disposed of by directing the consumer to appear before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.8, and the consumer does not appear on the date fixed, a later writ on the same cause of action seeking quashing of a subsequent notice and restoration of supply is not maintainable and will be dismissed without merits interference.
holding_units.flag: quoted earlier order treated a 'Katiya' theft allegation as remediable under Clause 6.8
